questions.scenario: Jamal approves GRN #GR-2026-0441 and a journal entry appears one second later. Who 'typed' it?
options: Shirin, working in the background
Nobody — the posting engine applied rule R1 to the approved document and wrote the entry automatically
The supplier's system posted it directly
An AI assistant watching the warehouse
questions.explanation: The engine is a rules machine: approved event in → pre-agreed rule → validated, balanced entry out. Humans approve events; the engine writes numbers.
wrongExplanations: The whole point of Module 4: no human types routine entries anymore.
Suppliers have no write access to Masco's books — only documents cross company borders.
There's no magic: it's deterministic configuration doing exactly what Shirin's team specified.

questions.scenario: Which four things does every posting rule define?
options: Color, icon, shortcut key, printer
Accounts (Dr/Cr), amounts, when allowed (sequence), which subledger rows
Only the debit account
Department, shift, machine, operator
questions.explanation: Those four answers fully determine an entry: where value goes, how much, whether reality permits it yet, and what detail rows accompany it.
wrongExplanations: UI cosmetics are not accounting logic.
A debit alone can't exist — Module 1 proved every entry needs both sides.
Those are production parameters, not posting logic.

questions.scenario: Someone requests payment to Delta Textile while their fabric GRN is still DRAFT. The engine must:
options: Post it — the entry would still balance
Refuse via sequence validation: payments require an APPROVED receipt first (R7 requires R1)
Post half now
Ask H&M for permission
questions.explanation: Balanced-but-impossible entries describe nothing real. Sequence checks enforce life's actual order: proof of goods received before money leaves.
wrongExplanations: 'It balances' was Rafiq's Module 1 mistake all over again — arithmetic isn't truth.
Partial posting of an invalid event doubles the fiction.
Buyers have nothing to do with supplier payments.

questions.scenario: Why should posting rules live in versioned CONFIGURATION rather than inside code?
options: Configuration files load faster
Account mappings are business decisions that change; config lets finance update them with change control, and each stored entry records WHICH rule version created it
Code cannot contain numbers
So developers can edit them silently
questions.explanation: Config separates WHAT the rule says from HOW it executes. Versioning gives auditability: any historical entry can show exactly the rule that produced it, even after updates.
wrongExplanations: Speed is irrelevant at this scale.
Code can hold anything — the issue is who may change business decisions and how traceably.
The opposite: config + change control REMOVES silent edits.

questions.scenario: During Step 6, the GL insert succeeds but the inventory lot row fails. A correct engine will:
options: Keep the GL entry and log a warning
Roll back EVERYTHING — GL and subledger writes happen atomically or not at all
Retry only the lot row tomorrow
Post the difference to Suspense
questions.explanation: Atomicity is Module 3's reconciliation promise enforced by engineering. Partial writes manufacture unexplainable mismatches — the exact disease this system exists to cure.
wrongExplanations: That creates an orphan entry with no detail rows — permanently unreconcilable.
Tomorrow the GL shows yarn that no subledger row explains; today's reports already lie.
Suspense accounts are for investigated timing differences, never for engineering failures.

questions.scenario: Yarn lot 2026-C-118 holds 5,000 kg. A floor request wants to ISSUE 6,000 kg from it. The engine:
options: Posts it and lets stock go negative as a signal
Rejects it — issuing beyond a lot's balance is physically impossible, so financially forbidden (quantity availability check on R2)
Issues 5,000 silently and posts 1,000 elsewhere
Converts the extra 1,000 kg to fabric automatically
questions.explanation: Sequence/feasibility validation protects reality: you cannot consume material that doesn't exist. The request itself signals a data error (wrong lot? wrong quantity?) that humans must resolve.
wrongExplanations: Negative stock hides theft and planning errors until they explode at physical count.
Silent splitting corrupts BOTH lots' histories and nobody learns the request was wrong.
Material conversion happens through PRODUCTION events (R3), not wishful issuance.

questions.scenario: One purchase arrives WITH recoverable VAT. How does the engine handle two consequences of one event?
options: Two separate unrelated entries
A multi-line entry composed by the rule: Dr Inventory + Dr VAT Input / Cr Supplier — all lines trace to the same source document
VAT must wait for month-end
The engine refuses mixed events
questions.explanation: Rules compose: one event, multiple lines, one balance check across all of them, one document reference shared. Multi-line entries are routine — payroll uses five+ lines.
wrongExplanations: Unlinked entries would break document traceability (Module 0's Golden Rule).
VAT input arises AT purchase time under accrual accounting; deferral misstates both asset and liability.
Mixed events are normal life — refusal would make the ERP useless.

questions.scenario: Jamal approved a GRN with quantity 500 instead of 5,000 (typo). The entry already posted. Correct remedy path:
options: Rafiq runs UPDATE on the journal line to fix the amount
Delete the journal entry quietly
Cancel/amend the GRN through its approval flow → engine posts the REVERSING/correcting entry; original stays intact forever
Ignore it — small amounts don't matter
questions.explanation: Documents are corrected through documents; entries follow. Reversal keeps the audit trail complete: anyone auditing sees what happened AND how it was fixed.
wrongExplanations: Direct edits destroy history — auditors treat edited ledgers as unreliable ledgers.
Deletion is the same crime with extra steps.
৳28 lakh of misstated inventory is neither small nor ignorable — and the PRINCIPLE matters more than the amount.

questions.scenario: Which design decision makes the engine's output trustworthy to AUDITORS years later?
options: Entries store which rule VERSION produced them, plus immutable audit log of approver/time/document reference
The engine has a nice UI
Rules are kept secret from staff
All entries post at midnight for consistency
questions.explanation: Traceability trinity: source document + rule version + human approval trail. Any figure can be walked backwards: entry → rule v7 → GR#GR-2026-0441 → Jamal's approval. That walk is what an audit IS.
wrongExplanations: Presentation doesn't create trustworthiness — lineage does.
Opacity is the opposite of auditability.
Timing uniformity means nothing about correctness.

questions.scenario: Shirin proposes adding a new event type: 'buyer claim approved → reduce revenue'. As ERP owner, your FIRST deliverable before any coding:
options: Let Rafiq pick reasonable accounts himself
Write the posting rule spec: exact Dr/Cr accounts, amount basis, sequence requirements (which documents must exist), subledger effects — then get finance sign-off
Skip rules; handle claims manually forever
Ask the buyer how they'd like it recorded
questions.explanation: This module's discipline: the RULE TABLE is the contract between business and engineering. Coding before the signed rule produces software that balances and lies.
wrongExplanations: Developers implement rules; deciding financial treatment is finance's accountability.
Manual handling reintroduces typos, inconsistency, and zero audit trail — backwards evolution.
Buyers don't set your chart of accounts or recognition policy.
